newsitem.title: USA: Oil prices, gold lower, coffee firm.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices, gold lower, coffee firm.

text.p: Crude and heating oil prices fell Tuesday as milder weather spread across the northern United States, but coffee prices rose again as traders worried about supplies from Colombia.
At the New York Mercantile Exchange, February heating oil closed 0.91 cent a gallon lower at 66.03 cents. February crude oil ended 43 cents a barrel lower at $24.80.

Meteorologists have called for above average temperatures this week in the Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world, just when cash traders have characterised heating oil supply as plentiful in the U.S. Gulf and New York Harbour.
"I really feel things with heating oil are over for now, and the next bull is gasoline," said Allendale Inc. trader James Cordier.
Gasoline bucked the downward trend. February unleaded gasoline rose 0.21 cent a gallon to 67.44 cents.
Unleaded gasoline prices in the U.S. Gulf refining region were up 1 cent a gallon from Monday as a slew of refinery maintenance shutdowns there added to demand, traders said.
Production from these refineries is expected to resume with an emphasis on gasoline as refiners stock up ahead of the spring and summer season when demand for gasoline traditionally peaks.

At New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange, coffee futures registered gains for a sixth straight session as a dockworkers' strike in Colombia and the prospect of a smaller Brazilian crop underpinned the market, traders said.
March coffee ran up to a new life-of-contract high of 130.80 cents a pound before settling at 129.65 cents, up 0.40 cent. Prices are up 25 percent in the last six weeks on supply worries.
Traders kept a wary eye on Colombia, the No. 2 coffee exporter, where dockworkers continued their strike at the Pacific coast port of Buenaventura.
That port handled 60 percent of Colombia's coffee shipments. The work stoppage, which entered its seventh day Tuesday, has blocked shipment of 145,000 bags of coffee exports.
Estimates for Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop this week have also dipped below 20 million bags, well below last season's 25 million bags.
New York precious metals futures gave back early gains to end mostly lower as the dollar remained firm and U.S. stocks markets saw new record highs.

Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gave Congress an upbeat assessment of the economy, allowing bond markets to recover ground and the stock market to push higher, meaning paper assets retained more attraction than gold, analysts said.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange's Comex division, February gold ended down 80 cents at $353.80, not far from the contract low at $352.60 seen on Jan. 15.
Comex March silver ended down 1.7 cent at $4.715 an ounce.
Spot gold slid to three-year lows at $352 an ounce in mid-January, after news of a 300 metric ton sale of gold by the Dutch central bank.
